title: Post-incident RCA: Dedicated pool throughput collapse during client surge
creator: Ava Chen
description: During a high-volume customer ingestion on 2026-03-01 evening we observed a sustained throughput collapse in a set of Dedicated GPU pools serving medium-latency workloads. Impact: several customers saw elevated latencies (>3x baseline) and request throttles for ~45 minutes before mitigations restored capacity. This ticket captures the root-cause analysis, short-term mitigations, and tracked action items to prevent recurrence.
root_cause_summary: Multiple contributing failures aligned: (1) a recent metrics change that switched autoscaler input to a custom histogram metric (inflight_requests_per_gpu_histogram) introduced bucket normalization drift under burst patterns, causing the HPA to undercount active load; (2) a runtime 1.19 kernel selection regression increased per-request GPU memory residency for certain model variants, accelerating KV cache eviction and increasing request tail latency; (3) autoscaler cooldown and replica caps were conservative and prevented fast recovery during the surge.
timeline: 2026-03-01T18:05Z - Traffic spike begins from Customer X (large batch inference burst).
2026-03-01T18:12Z - Datadog alert: sustained queue depth increase for dedicated-pool-eu-west-1. Latency SLO breach triggered.
2026-03-01T18:20Z - Autoscaler did not begin adding replicas as expected due to histogram metric reporting falling below scale threshold.
2026-03-01T18:28Z - Engineering on-call initiated emergency fallback: route lower-priority tenants to shared pools and enabled emergency-burst pool (manual).
2026-03-01T19:00Z - Temporary mitigations restored throughput to ~85% of baseline; full recovery by 19:50Z after cache warmup and manual replica increases.
mitigations_taken: Manual tenant throttling and reroute to shared-hosted API (mitigated customer impact).
Created emergency hot pool (manual) and increased replica count for affected Dedicated pools.
Rolled back autoscaler metric source to CPU + request_rate hybrid for affected pools as a temporary guard.
Scoped quick rollback of the kernel selector change for the most-affected model variant (runtime-1.19 -> runtime-1.18) to reduce memory pressure.
long_term_action_items: ENG-48905: Normalize histogram-based custom metrics at ingestion to stable rate buckets; owner: Priya Raman; due: 2026-03-31.
ENG-48906: Add synthetic surge canary and blackbox test in CI that replays burst patterns and validates autoscaler response time; owner: Diego Morales; due: 2026-04-07.
ENG-48907: Implement autoscaler smoothing that uses median+95p window to avoid underscaling on bursty histograms; owner: Martin Schulz; due: 2026-04-14.
ENG-48908: Add deterministic fallback policy in routing: if pool headroom < X% for 30s, reroute lower-priority traffic to compatible smaller model variant; owner: Sarah Patel; due: 2026-04-21.
ENG-48909: Kernel selector safety net: auto-detect runtime kernel regressions by validating memory-residency on canary nodes before wide rollout; owner: Applied ML team (Alex Wu); due: 2026-04-14.
ENG-48910: Update Dedicated runbook with emergency headroom pool creation steps and SLA-preserving throttles; owner: Oncall WG (Rotating); due: 2026-03-24.
